description: Aggregation queries — GROUP BY, HAVING, aggregate functions

cases.natural_language: What is the total revenue by product category?
cases.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category

cases.natural_language: Which categories have more than 100 orders?
cases.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) > 100

cases.natural_language: Show me the average, minimum, and maximum order total by month
cases.expected_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS month, AVG(total) AS avg_total, MIN(total) AS min_total, MAX(total) AS max_total FROM orders GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) ORDER BY month
cases.description: Multiple aggregate functions with temporal grouping

cases.natural_language: What percentage of total revenue does each category represent?
cases.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS category_revenue, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(quantity * unit_price) FROM order_items), 2) AS revenue_percentage FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY category_revenue DESC

cases.natural_language: Count how many orders are above and below average order value
cases.expected_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM orders) THEN 'Above Average' ELSE 'Below Average' END AS category, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY CASE WHEN total > (SELECT AVG(total) FROM orders) THEN 'Above Average' ELSE 'Below Average' END
cases.description: Conditional aggregation with CASE and subquery
